text: These are Paul's Stuffed Cheese Pizza for $17.49 and the Garlic Parm Poppers for $4.79 at Paul's Chicago Pizza in Saint Petersburg. Stop it, autocorrect, they are not called "poopers." I've heard so much about Paul from you guys that my pal and I just had to go and meet him. Does he really pack those pizzas thick? Are they the real Chicago deal or is Paul actually from Albuquerque? Some native Chicago peeps here have blasted them while everyone else sings Paul's praises, so we went to find out and settle this once and for all. We were greeted by a man who was relaxing in a booth two over to the left. We assumed he was a patron before he gestured at the tables and told us to sit anywhere we'd like. We did so and we were greeted within a minute by a kind server who presented us with menus and took our drink orders. I must say that this server (I wish I remembered her name but my memory problems struck again) was fantastic. She was ecstatic about the food and made personal recommendations based on her own and popular preferences regardless of price. She suggested the garlic parm poppers and we had to get them. Naturally, we also ordered their namesake - a Chicago-style stuffed cheese pizza. I'm used to Giordano's where the pizzas take 45 minutes to bake and there is no ordering ahead. I went there, ready to kill the whole day, so imagine my surprise when the garlic poppers came out about 5 minutes after we ordered them and the pizza came out 15 minutes after that. We commented on it and our server explained that unlike Giordano's, their pizza is only served medium, so that likely attributes to the cooking time. Seeing as there were only two of us, medium was more than enough. She did seem to have a bit of friendly competition when I mentioned their larger competitor, which we enjoyed! It made for friendly banter and showed her loyalty to the brand. They must treat her well and I support any establishment that treats their people well. Onto the grub. The garlic parm poppers were a delight. Three words that come to mind are "fluffy," "cheesy," and "bouncy." The poppers were baked brown on one side and light on the other, creating a pleasant dichotomy of consistencies. Each popper was just enough to cradle your tongue around and savor the garlic oil and Parmesan drizzled on top. The garlic did not have a spicy bite to it the way fresh chopped garlic does, which was nice to me because no one appreciates that level of garlic breath, but that's just a matter of preference. The marinara sauce was bright and refreshing, coating each popper in an incredibly satisfying way and completing the experience by making sure the bread goes down smooth. The first thing to notice about the pizza is that cheese pull. Did you see that cheese pull? Go check out that cheese pull. Don't worry, I'll wait. Saw it? Good. That cheese pull gets a 20 out of 5. The freshness was off the charts on this one - it had to have literally come straight out of the oven. The vapor exploded out in a cloud of mozzarella essence that prepared us for the deliciousness to come. The cheese was the star, filling the bite with a rich creamy gentle saltiness that pairs well with the tomato sauce on top. The sauce itself, I felt could use a bit more seasoning (and the crust could use a LOT of seasoning), but it wasn't anything to really ruin anything for me. After all, I had that marinara from the poppers to dip the crust in. One thing that did mess with the taste of that pizza, however, was the BOTTOM crust of the pizza. I don't know what it was, perhaps the flour that the pizza sat on before/during baking? Whatever it was, that very thin layer of dough had a very distinct and cutting yeast note that permeated the rest of the flavors, causing my blissful reaction to end with a question mark. The main goal was to get stabilization from medication, something we had not been able to do with outpatient or acute inpatient treatment. Aside from one wonderful therapist named Heather, friendly cafeteria staff, and a few compassionate techs on the boys' hall, the staff was awful. The psychiatrist called him the wrong first name the entire stay and did not listen to our concerns regarding medication. We did not get his medication stabilized until we brought him home, weaned him off the medications prescribed at Willow Springs, and worked with an outpatient doctor. I mostly chose to give the 5-stars, instead of 4-stars because of the hospitality we received from the server/bartender, Kieran! Walking into the place, we didn't know quite what to expect. The photos online (Google & Yelp) looked amazing! This is primarily the reason my girl & I decided to meet our friend here for a late lunch. To our surprise though, there were only a few people inside the restaurant when we walked in. Kieran, who was behind the bar, talking to the only people inside, paused his conversation to greet us & led us to our table. Kieran was very welcoming, friendly, patient & knowledgeable of the menu! When we asked questions regarding menu items, he knew the ingredients, flavor profile & portion sizes. He even recommended a few dishes to us when we asked & even gave us a little inside info about where the chef was from & inspirations for a few dishes. We started of with 2 appetizers - the duck fries & Cajun cheese curds. They were so good, that when we placed our entree orders we, also, put in for more cheese curds & brussel sprouts! We savored each bite & took our time with the appetizers. The food came out right on time, within a few minutes after we finished our second round of appetizers. I got the "Tenderloin Frites" (one of Kieran's recommendations), served with duck fries - yes, duck fries again! - & both of the ladies got the "Meatloaf Wellington." As fans of family-style eating (you try more of the menu that way) we all shared & trades bites. Kieran checked up on us periodically to make sure everything was going well, & to fill up our waters. After the entrees we asked to see a dessert menu & deliberated on whether or not to get dessert, & which dessert to choose. After a few minutes Kieran returned & we asked his opinion once again. Immediately he said the "Wild Turkey Irish Cream Panna Cotta Brownie," which is the main one we were torn between. To be honest, the dessert came out & we laughed. It was so much smaller than we anticipated, but we were soon silenced. Hahaha. The caramel & brownie were so rich & delicious we found ourselves taking smaller, slower bites in order enjoy it longer. Lol. Compliments to the chef on everything we ordered from start to finish!!! On the way out, I spoke to manager, Derek (not sure if that's spelled correctly), & he was very friendly. Told him about our experience & praised our server, & he thanked us for coming & enthusiastically invited us back! ...Will definitely return!

Most of the plants were in great shape and health - colors of all sorts bursting in every corner. There was quite an eclectic collection of tropical flowers as well. However, it's all pretty expensive in comparison to similar assortments you can get down the road at Pickering Valley. That said, Gardner's had a lot more variety. It also doesn't hurt to check out the inner shop within the greenhouse. They've got a nice selection of tea and a lot of other interesting, decorative items for sale. text: Let me start this review by saying that Jeff Ruby's steakhouse is an upscale dining restaurant. With that said, suite coat attire is not necessary but you will see some patrons wearing them. I was unsure leading up to my dining experience so I wore one. There were also patrons wearing nice jeans and button up shirts. I would not wear less than that for you may feel inadequately dressed. Now I'll begin my review. Tonight's dinner in Nashville was highly hyped up. And it delivered in full. Jeff Ruby's from its appetizers to dessert were exceptional. The complementary bread with their truffle butter was unique but delicious. Next we had a sushi appetizer, the music city roll. The fish was fresh and the combined ingredients caused an explosion of flavor. Lastly for appetizers, the wedge salad that we split was HUGE, the bacon was extra thick and the blue cheese dressing was abundant. For our main entree we split the 24oz porterhouse. The steak was cooked to a mouth watering perfect medium rare. The staff was nice enough to split it in the back so we could easily enjoy the steak. The steak was still oozing juice when served table side. The seasoning used with the steak was exceptional. Truly cooked and seasoned to perfection where no condiment were needed to aid in flavor. The two sides that we chose were the Mack and cheese and the Nashville hot greens. Both were delicious, the Mac and cheese was exceptional. The Nashville greens have a bit of heat which make you go back for more. Lastly, my wife's favorite part of the meal, the desert. It was the well known and huge Jack Daniels chocolate truffle cake. It was exceptionally moist with a light hint of Jack Daniels. Nothing to deter from, it was extremely mild and had a unique taste. So far, on this first visit to Nashville I can say confidently that this has been our favorite place to dine! I would also recommend reservations as this place gets really busy!

text: It's difficult to put into words what's been so frustrating about Hello Donuts so far - a place that is very local to where I live, and should be a welcome addition to the neighborhood, but I'll try to just go in order of the things that frustrate me every time I stop by. 1. Fillings for donuts are far, far too wet. When you have a Nutella filled donut that you're enthusiastically advertising on your Instagram, thoughts of that thick, pleasantly creamy Nutella texture take over and one expects the donut to live up to them - instead, it's akin to trying to eat soup out of a bread bowl that you're holding in your hand in your car on your way to work. 2. The service is not particularly engaged, considering how infrequently the place is busy when I've come in. Asking for a coffee with "no room" is immediately understood in Reanimator, because they ask you every time otherwise whether you want room for cream and sugar. At Hello, they'll just assume you want an 80% filled cup of coffee, then walk away immediately. I don't need to be fawned over by any stretch of the imagination, but some level of engagement with the coffee part of the business would be greatly appreciated. 3. The amount of vegan options are commendable, but sometimes flavors that would simply taste better with dairy (chocolate covered donuts particularly) are always vegan, and always suffer as a result. 4. I realize that if people aren't knocking down the doors, it's tough to offer fresh, warm donuts - but considering the condition of some by the time it's later in the day, rotating them would be something that would keep people who aren't early risers more satisfied with the offerings. The knock on Hello before they had a brick and mortar was that by the time donuts were delivered to outposts, they weren't particularly fresh tasting any longer - and it's a shame to see that happening with the location of the baking process itself. There are good things though! There's the shell of a very nice little coffee shop. But when you're a couple of blocks from Reanimator, which partially owns Hello if I understand correctly, there's very little reason to go to Hello unless you just badly need a donut. I'm always just left wishing I'd gone to Reanimator and traded a pretty good yeast donut (something that this city still lacks, since Federal just makes incredibly dry and crumbly cake donuts that are the most overrated donuts perhaps in the whole country) for an excellent all-around experience. I think Hello will still potentially get there, and I'll update this review if they do.

text: You don't spend $120 on a pair of leggings because they are that amazing, because they aren't, you are buying a brand and the experience that goes with it. This store crushes the brand experience consistently and for that, they have lost a longtime customer. I've had two catastrophic experiences here, the rest have been unfriendly, but not noteworthy. Not once in the 5 years that I have been coming here have I ever been greeted when entering the store, not once has someone been friendly and asked if there was anything they could help me with. The experience you should expect is to be ignored and feel less than or not included in the "cool kids club", basically what I am saying is that I should have stopped coming here a long time ago, but became immune to the toxic environment. I sent my mom to get a pair of pants and return a sweater for me (that she bought online on her card) over Christmas time, she had never been in and I simply gave her the name of the pants. She found an employee and asked where she could find the pant and was pointed in the direction of several shelves by someone who said "if there are any left, they are over there." She asked if the employee could show her what they were as she didn't know what they looked like, they employee said something like it would be a minute, and walked away. My mom said it was so uncomfortable and the employee made her feel like she didn't belong in there so instead of trying to find the pants she just went to complete my return. She had an equally poor experience during the return, the register attendant did not want to take the return and said she needed to find something to exchange it with, the issue being that the item was for me and I wasn't there. She was accused of having worn the item, yes I tried it on, but never wore it around, it was simply too big. She ended up walking away frustrated and having not been able to return the item. She told me to never ask for a gift from Lululemon again because she refused to ever spend another dollar there. I went in the following day ready for a battle as I had tried on, but not worn the sweater, there was no issue and it was returned. I had wondered at the time if my mom exaggerated the situation or just didn't want to return for me, but after my recent experience I can absolutely understand now. I also bought her two pair of the pant I had told her to get, because they were great. I love the versatility of the "On The Move" pant which is equal parts comfort and style. You'll find most all of my co-workers with a pair. I went in the store on Women's Day as they advertised 18% off everything, per usual, no greeting when I walked in. I collected several items to try on (never approached once during my shopping by an employee) and then went to the fitting room area where a large group of people were huddled around the table and talking. I wasn't sure where to stand as there was no line and it appeared maybe a room or two was available. I awkwardly stood where I thought a line should form and waited for an employee to approach me, it was over 5 minutes before I was first approached by one of the employees who had been standing directly behind me chatting with other employees and some of their friends. She asked if I needed a fitting room and I told her I did, she said they were all taken. I continued waiting while what seemed to be a friend group would come in and out of the dressing rooms, talking with employees and asking for recommendations, talking about discounts etc. The people in the dressing rooms would leave all their things in the room, go shop and come back with several additional items all while I continued waiting. This is not how dressing rooms work.. you don't get to camp out and make others wait while you come and go as if this is your own personal shopping experience and no other customers matter. I was extremely disappointed that the employees continued to allow this to happen. But hey, they seemed to all be friends and it sounded like they were sharing their employee discount, so why would a full price paying customer matter anyhow? I finally said something and the employee replied that the customer was just grabbing something else, as if I was out of line to even ask to get in a room again. I ended up putting my pile down and walking away. I was so mad and like my mom, decided to be done supporting this Lululemon. I ended up calling the corporate number as I was so frustrated by my experience and I believe my frustrations were taken seriously, I received an email from the store manager who said she would be addressing with her team and she even gave me a $30 coupon for future use. I still am mad because this seems to be the normal etiquette.

text: Ambience: A little crowded and small indoor dining area, but the real star is the outdoor seating area! It's very beautiful, not too crowded, homey yet modern. There's a fireplace and multiple heat lamps to keep you warm during the night as well. Wine: I had two different types of red based on their recommendations and both were delicious! The servers really knew the flavors of the wine as their descriptions fit the taste perfectly! El Bulli Olive: Didn't really know what to expect, but it seemed interesting and fun to eat. It's one of those molecular gastronomy food items where it imitates the real thing. It popped in my mouth and had an olive flavored juice. Interesting and tasted decent, but probably would not order again. Jamon tasting: This was probably the highlight specifically because of the jamon iberico bellota, the acorn fed pig ham. I've always seen it on shows and to finally taste it was amazing, it lived up to the hype and anticipation. It was rich, nutty, melty, salty deliciousness. I'd say it's a must try if you come here. The bread it comes with was warm and fresh, which makes a big difference for me in the quality of a restaurant! Tortilla Espanola: Tasted better than I expected! It's creamy, savory, and hearty with the meat and potatoes. Can't go wrong with this. Medulla/Bone marrow: The executive chef is Korean and the bone marrow tasted almost exactly like jjajangmyeon, a fermented black bean noodle dish very common in Korea. Overall, tasted good, the jjajang/flavoring was very strong however and could not taste any beefiness of the marrow. Brussel sprouts: Their variation of the brussel sprouts is pretty good, I really like the combination of their sauce and the dates. Overall I'd highly recommend this place for a romantic date or nicer outing with friends/family. I'll definitely have to come back to try everything else especially the paella!

The portion size and amount of shrimp is unreal, as in at least 2 more meals. The garlic bread is just about the best I've ever had...by the way I'm an original Long Islander. Their New England clam chowder was thick, hot, and full of clams and packed with flavor. The lobster bisque was everything you would expect...rich, flavorful, and hearty. My husband was blown away by the way the potatoes contributed to the amazing texture of the soup. Speaking of my husband, he ordered the lobster bake. My parents ordered fried oysters and fried belly clams, which they each raced over. The batter was flavorful and not saturated in grease. They also had coleslaw, fries, and onion rings. text: I realized just now that I haven't reviewed my favorite Vietnamese restaurant in the treasure valley. Pho Bac is a close second but Baguette has been our go-to for 8 years or more. The pho is excellent and flavorful. The banh mi are made with bread baked at the Asian market a few blocks away and that bread is light with a perfect crispy crust that is kind of old school-- lighter than some of the heavier artisanal baguettes one has come to expect from fancy bakeries. The mayonnaise is perfect and I have come to order the beef usually, with crunchy carrot and cucumber and jalapeño making them little bites of clean fresh power goodness. What are the negatives? There is only one kind of pho. I would personally appreciate having a bottle of sriracha on the table instead of the 50-50 hoisin/sriracha condiment containers served with the pho. The cha gio are precooked and therefore room temperature. And the menu still has beignets even though they aren't available, and haven't been for many years. Additionally, bun thit nuong is reportedly on the menu but it's not on the marquee menu on the wall so I never order it, even though this dish is a huge mainstay for me in Vietnamese food. But Baguette has delivered for me for a long time and I reward its consistency and high quality main dishes with the Royal 5 Star Medal of Grant.

Let your customers know what's going on-- instead, the staff avoided making eye contact. Remove signage that is incorrect. If a room isn't used for overflow take off the sign that says it is. We would never have waited in line as long as we did had we known how the system works. I guess that might be the point as more people might walk out rather than face a long wait. Had I known up front I would have left, but also would have given it another shot; now if anyone asks me what I think of the London Tea Room my answer will be to stay away. text: Michael Solomonov team has done it again. Man oh man, is K'Far worth the visit. Zahav is by far our favorite restaurant, so we had to try K'Far out ASAP. We arrived ~11:30ish on Labor Day, so it was a little crowded, and they had run out of a few items, so just keep that in mind if visiting later in the day. For eats, we both got the grilled cheese on the Jersualem bagel (my BF wanted the egg and cheese, but had run out). This was a great spin on a classic grilled cheese - with kashkaval cheese instead of American, roasted tomato, and za'atar, we were definitely vibing with the Israeli flavors. We attempted to order the pistachio sticky buns and chocolate babka, but unfortunately, they were both out. Instead, we chose the tehina chocolate chip cookie and the chocolate rugelach (which they wound up giving complimentary). The cookie was delightful, very dense with just a hint of the tehina flavor to cut the sweetness a tad. The rugelach were surprisingly delicious as well - often, I find this pastry dry, but K'Far's take was incredibly moist and chock-ful of chocolate flavor, so definitely proving me wrong! Lastly, I tried the Yemenite latte and my BF had the cappuccino. I'm not usually one to order "fancy" drinks, but I am SO glad I did - this latte was devine, so creamy and delicious with unique flavors of cardamon, cinnamon, and ginger. The cappuccino was tasty too, but would 100% recommend the Yemenite latte :) To top off our great experience, Michael Solomonov himself was actually serving and delivering food to tables! We had to do a double take to make sure it was actually him, but indeed was. He delivered our food, so we got to snag a pic with him and chat for a few. A very humble and kind dude, and so cool that he gets to hang at K'Far by day and Zahav by night. K'Far did not disappoint, and we are so excited to try the Solomonov team's other upcoming endeavors. And I'm already looking forward to another K'Far visit for that latte and some of their other pastries :)

text: tl;dr don't expect authentic dim sum -- a trendy, industrial vibe and twists on traditional favorites define this Asian-American fusion bar From the group behind Cheu Noodles, Bing Bing Dim Sum takes quintessential dim sum and turns it on its head. The space itself channels red tones and trendy industrial vibes throughout an intimate room. Colorful lights illuminate the street art that is graffitied along the walls. The restaurant is abuzz with chatter, and multiple people brush past the back of your chair as they navigate the borderline-cramped walkways. Eccentrically shaped tables are custom-fit to the space, and the booths sit beneath personal pagodas. Intricate details are sprinkled throughout the room from hand-painted lamps to customized window decals. My partner and I reserved a table for 5:15PM on a Friday -- just in time for happy hour. By the time we arrived, the restaurant was in full force, and we were escorted to the final available table. For drinks, I went with the Tired Hands pilsner on draft, my partner picked out the Milk Money cocktail. Then, we opted for an assortment of dim sum offerings: the Pickle Plate, the Cheesesteak Bao, the Mongolian Beef Dumplings, the Scarlet Dumplings, and the Caterpillar Bread. The dishes filed out as they were prepared, and our table quickly filled up with a myriad of aromatic plates. The pickle platter consisted of carrots, green beans, kimchi, and roasted nuts -- a nice amuse-bouche, but nothing to write home about. The bao were stuffed with ribeye, cooper sharp, and long hots, with a richness perfectly complemented by sweet plum sauce. The beef dumplings were decorated with chimichurri and crispy onions -- yet, they were essentially indistinguishable from your run-of-the-mill pan-fried variety. The veggie dumplings, on the other hand, were coiled in a vibrant beet wrapper; while the texture was slightly less crisp, this dish was the freshest and least greasy vegetarian takes on dumplings I've had the pleasure to try. Finally, the caterpillar bread had the fluffiness of bao, but was drizzled with a just-less-than-overwhelming caramelized honey syrup to perfectly contrast the rich and salty barbequed pork filling. Bing Bing is fun, and, true to the restaurant group, doesn't take itself to seriously. My major gripe is that cocktails are beyond expensive -- during happy hour, my pint ran me $5, while my partner's drink soared upwards of $10! To put it in other words, would you rather have 1 drink or 4 cheesesteak bao? Nonetheless, with a bevy of yummy, cheap food offerings, I see myself coming back here very soon.

So I likely won't be returning...and since the same chef owns Cork and Cow, 55 South, and others, that includes those establishments as well. My time is too valuable to me to waste on a bad experience. Chef, once again, classic dishes are classics for a reason. You may think you're talented and creative and all that, but you can't improve upon a classic, so don't try. You just end up ruining it. Setting *** Small little place that resembles a house with a small parking lot, inside it's a garish blend of colors and signs. It's relatively clean but I I'm not sure it's that well maintained. Little things bothered me like the half empty Salt and Pepper shakers and the grime around the bathroom door handle. I think they may have a heating issue since on a chilly Sunday morning it was very cold inside and I did see a space heater in one section but it wasn't on. There are picnic tables outside. Service *** You order fast food style at counter and they bring the food out to you. The cook/cashier wasn't particularly friendly but he did his job. Food ** Not entirely awful but I'm certainly not running back for it. My daughters hot dog was very pale in color, a bun that felt like it cane out of a freezer it was so cold and she thought it tasted gross. She also thought her milkshake was disgusting and threw it away after a few sips. My Bacon Cheeseburger was ok after a couple of bites but it tasted unseasoned, was well done and was missing the Wimpys Sauce I requested. Our shared French Fries were probably the best thing we had but the first few had an odd burnt taste to them. Value ** It's not too bad but for the quality it feels expensive to me. My burger at starting at $5.75 then add another $1.50 for the toppings, adding in fries was another $3.50. Two for lunch was $22.
label: NEG

text: The Hank's Manifesto By Dr M Herzberg A neighborhood can be compared to a living organism. Its streets are the veins, its homes are the skin, its trees and plants are the lungs, and its many varied inhabitants are the brain and central nervous system. But as any scientist (such as myself) can tell you, no organism can survive without a heart. In the case of the organism that is the Marigny/Bywater, Hank's fulfills that role. This is true on a physical level: Hank's moves our bloodstream by providing it with precious resources such as 40's of malt beverages, corn dogs, "tobacco" pipes, Roquefort cheese, canned beans, etcetera. But more importantly, Hank's is the neighborhood's spiritual heart. People come to Hank's from all walks of life to heal, to escape the nihilist horror and alienation which day-to-day life in our capitalist society inevitably accompany. Hank's cares not whether you have won today's battle with your inner daemons or whether guilt and shame consumes you. Hank's is here for you to listen, without judgement, and to bless your broken soul. Yes, they were allegedly anti-semites, back in days of yore. That's a big no-no. But this era of hatred has passed, as the employees who perpetrated these vile injustices have been tried and punished in the international court of Hank's. The banality of evil has been replaced with the totality of love and understanding. The new Hankers are people of honor and integrity, and they will hold your head on their bosoms and sing their sweet lullabies as you weep your tears of sorrow, washing away years of emotional repression and resentment. The pressing question remains: who is Hank? Is Hank the owner who benevolently smiles at us from his hidden palace? Is Hank the lady who makes the fried chicken in disguise? Is Hank the crusty in the parking lot who asks you for 47 cents? Hank remains a misunderstood figure, because in truth, there is no one Hank. Hank is an ethereal concept: we are all Hank. As such I invite you to see for yourself the greatest organization in this country, nay, on this planet. Be it for an afternoon shrimp po-boy (with extra hot sauce) or a handjob in the parking lot (not officially endorsed by Hank's, but they'll provide you with lube and napkins), come and awaken your inner ubermensch as you do away with the corpse of Judeo-Christian morality and see the truth beyond good and evil: Hank.

text: "A dealer for the people and on a mission to put the fun back into buying a car and treat our customers with the respect they deserve", I am not too sure of that... A few weeks ago we went there shopping for a car for my son, first time young buyer, no credit, etc... After discussing the desired monthly payment, current down payment, no co-signer, the sales person was nice and anxious to get my son approved. We were given only 1 car option, the sales person took us to a car and said "this is it". I asked if there were other cars for us to see, he repeated "this is it, this is the one". Didn't offer for us to test drive it. Okay then! We said. Since my son was in a desperate need for a car, he went for it after agreeing on the monthly payment. At this time I expressed my concern about some reviews (people mentioned the drove off with car then later asked to return the car) we wanted to be really sure he was 100% approved before we drove off with a car, the sales person and manager reassured us this would not happen, after all they had all the info they needed, 1 month worth of payroll stubs, credit report, down payment, references, etc... And so he was "Approved"! Heck, they even played the 'Happy' song by Pharell Williams, had him hit the bell while all the employees cheered on, lots of happy tears were shed that day.... Signed papers and off we went with a newly purchased car. About 1 week later the sales man (Mr. Fudge) called me asking if I could co-sign for my son, I reminded him that we made it super clear before we agreed to anything that my son would be the only one on the loan and they said he was approved with no co-signer. Mr. Fudge said he wasn't approved otherwise... I told him we would take car back then since that was one of our conditions in the first place. Mr. Fudge quickly hung up without even saying bye. What happened to the treating people 'courteously' part of the mission? Mr. Fudge then called my son while he was at work, with a 'hey buddy, you need a co-signer, if you don't have one, you need to bring back the car" sounded more like the repo man at this point (maybe not exact lingo, but started with "hey buddy" not professional at all... ) What happened to the "dealer for the people" and to "treat customers with respect" part of the mission? As soon as my son got home from work, we returned the car to the dealer where they claim to put the fun back into things, we felt sort of a relief at this point, because we didn't really choose the car, they chose it for us and them being so rude now, we didn't want anything from them. About a week after returning the car we get a congratulatory letter from the bank with details about the loan and monthly payment due date. It turns out, my son was approved and we did not have to return the car, the bank had already funded the deal!!! Yet we had to go through all the unnecessary heartache and distress of having to return the car, the memories of the 'Happy" song, hitting the bell, knowing what it feels like to have a repo man call you and demand the car back... all so much to take in, so many tears... I gave it 1 star, because when I called the dealer about the last pickle situation, the manager Cory (I believe it was) was very nice, he called me when he was already off work, he reassured me he knew exactly which deal this was and that he would refund the bank the money and close out the loan account. He did just that. We take some responsibility, we went there despite hearing all the annoying commercials, so it was our punishment for not trusting our gut. On a positive note, we ended up going to JC, got to test drive several cars, and we got to choose a nicer car, with slightly better terms, maybe this whole situation was Mother Nature's way of relieving us from a pickled situation.

text: If you've never been to a Chinese bakery, you'll love the experience from seeing and smelling all the yummy buns, cookies, and tarts! When you're ready, you just bring your tray to the register and they'll box it for you. There are more choices in the display case next to the register which has all the refrigerated cakes, cheesecakes, mousses, etc. They also have additional items (noodle soups, coffee, congee, etc.) on the menu board, but I think that's limited during covid. As far as buns, you won't go wrong with anything. You MUST try the pineapple bun - the only place that has real pineapples in the bun. Egg tarts are yummy and flaky, but as usual, heavy in butter/fat. There's some more unique stuff like taro buns or lotus almond buns. Go for it and try it! The ingredients are usually just some form of sweetener like bean paste or vegetable. If you like things that aren't too sweet, then you'll have to try their birthday cakes. These are typical Chinese fruit cakes - a light vanilla sponge cake with layers of fruit and cream (like cool whip) in between. Chinese people LOVE these (all my family at least lolol). Try the regular, then try taro or mango. They start at $35 for larger sizes, but you might be able to purchase a small slice from the case. It is a little pricier than a regular hole in the wall Chinese bakery, but it's worth it. Enjoy!

Then the lovely girl up front asked us if we would like a menu to look at to make it easier. We both decided on the Cuban Sandwich. The only difference is that my husband had his sandwich hot pressed and I didn't. We ordered our sandwiches, got some drinks, and sat at a table while we waited for our sandwiches to be ready. The sandwiches were large and we both ate only half. We needed to save room for dessert! I now know for next time to order half of my sandwich to be wrapped to go. But don't worry, they are very accommodating and gave me a piece of Saran Wrap when I asked. They also have bags out for your convenience. To finish off our lunch my hubby had a slice of Peanut Butter Chocolate Cake with a coffee and I had a Hawaiian Princess Cupcake. The slices of cake are huge! They are definitely the better value for the money. A huge slice of cake is $5.50 and a cupcake is $3.25. I finished my cupcake and my hubby took half his cake home to eat later with the other half of his sandwich. I ordered another cupcake to take home for later!! It was one of the best tasting cupcakes I've had in a long time. It was a delicious moist coconut cake with coconut and pineapple filling and a cream cheese frosting. OMG....It's definitely my absolute new favorite! Also, addition to the soda machines, they have several flavors of fresh brewed iced tea to choose from which was very good. The dining room was extremely large and there were plenty of seating of both booths and tables. Also, there were tables outside. All in all, the food was delicious, the tea was delicious , the staff was all friendly and attentive, the restaurant was clean and the dessert was to die for. I am pretty sure we'll be back to try another sandwich and I will need my Hawaiian Princess fix!! Take my advice and try a sandwich but don't forget to save room for the amazing desserts!!! Flounder, she intimated, was another possible choice, but because that day's catch was very expensive and very flattened, suggesting it would curl up in cooking, the mahi was, according to the chef, the better choice. Because they obviously didn't want to overcook it, it was soft and gooey inside, not at all reminiscent of the more familiar cod or haddock that is the generally accepted choice. The chips were wholly unimpressive--the skinniest shoestring potatoes I've ever seen, and again, unconventional when one is expecting a steakhouse fry for the chips, which is pretty universally considered the chip to accompany the fried fish. The tartar sauce was very good, and I assume made on premises, containing just the right amount of pickle and onion. Another diner in my party had the mini burgers--very small sliders. Sauce on the chicken wasn't bad, but if you cut the chicken in half, you'll notice that there's literally no texture. It's like an opaque pink. I'm sure they boiled it or something. I'm writing this about 12 hours after having eaten there and I feel fine. It was just really gross looking. The egg rolls weren't much better. The outside was crispy, but the inside was so soggy. I don't know how long everything is left out before it's replaced, but it just didn't seem food safe. I spent about $18 in all, which is a lot for food. I could have gone to a nice restaurant for $18. I'm sure they had the price posted somewhere, but I never saw it, I'd recommend making it more visible. My friend chose this place for his birthday, which is why I went. I forgot to get pictures, I was just really distracted by how disappointing the experience was. I really can't recommend this in good conscience, for so many reason. I've never run a restaurant before, but if I were the owner, here are a few things I'd do: * Don't make good until it needs to be made. The less it sits out, the better. * Use better ingredients. I know what you're thinking, "Aidan, those cost money, and we need money to keep things running." I know, but I'm so sure the extra money spent would be made more than made back if you had good food. The restaurant looked good enough on the inside, and the service was super friendly, just work on improving the food. One last thing for the management if they see this. I recommend you allow people to tip extra. Parties of 10 or more tip 15% by default. I didn't have cash and couldn't tip more. I recommend keeping 15% the minimum, but adding an area to tip more. It doesn't cost anything, and your servers will thank you.

Finally the repair was completed and bike was tested before being returned to us. The service manager came and spoke to my son and I. He was thankfully gracious and actually listened to us. He tried explaining in technical terms why they felt this could not have been the fault of the store but at least he was kind and listened and apologized which was really all we wanted to hear from the start of this whole mess. I don't know much about the mechanisms of bikes but I do know the frickin pedals should stay on when they have been installed by a service tech. So a brand new bike whose pedals were installed at the store at time of purchase and was serviced immediately before the pedal blew off somehow had this happen due to something we apparently did even though I repeatedly assured the owner we did not touch the bike other than to ride it a few times.
